raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
- `build.sh`: nightlies and branch builds reuse only `rocm/vllm-ci` images and cache, never read back `rocm/vllm-dev`, and write no cache of their own
- `build.sh`: the trust comment says the `pr<N>-`/`br-` prefixes keep names apart but isolate nothing, and that the per-commit test image is still pulled by tag
- `Dockerfile.rocm`: a new `csrc-inputs` stage hands the csrc compile only what `setup.py` reads from `pyproject.toml` and `envs.py`, and fails the build if the filtered `envs.py` would change a value `setup.py` reads
- `test_rocm_build.py`: only PR builds read back their own namespace, and nightlies still reuse `rocm/vllm-ci` images and cache

Every untrusted build pushes with the same `rocm/vllm-dev` credentials, so any PR could plant the `br-` images or cache an AITER nightly would reuse. Nightlies now take only what `rocm/vllm-ci` has. When a nightly's stack or runtime key is main's and CI has not pushed it yet, it waits for main's build of it (#63949) and builds it itself only if none is running; a branch whose stack or runtime inputs differ from main's now rebuilds them on every build. The nightly's per-commit test image is still pulled from `rocm/vllm-dev` by tag, and PR builds share the agents' buildkitd cache mounts with trusted builds as before, so both are left for ci-infra. Separately, 67 of the 240 commits on main that changed a csrc input over the last 60 days touched only `pyproject.toml` or `envs.py`, and each one recompiled all HIP code; replayed through the new filter, none of them changes the csrc inputs anymore. Follow-up to #61939; with main (and #63949) merged in, `pytest tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py` passes 41 tests in 10 runs out of 10.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

detail.title: [ROCm][CI] Keep nightlies off PR-writable images and trim the csrc cache key

files.patch:
@@ -22,10 +22,16 @@
 # Trust: ROCM_CI_REPO is set by ci-infra (CI) or release-pipeline.yaml (release).
 #   Trusted main builds: rocm/vllm-ci
 #   PR / fork builds:    rocm/vllm-dev    (pr<N>- tags and caches; trusted builds never read it)
-#   Other untrusted:     rocm/vllm-dev    (br-<branch>-<hash>- tags and caches: nightlies, branch builds)
+#   Other untrusted:     rocm/vllm-dev    (br-<branch>-<hash>- tags: nightlies, branch builds; they
+#                                          push these but never read them back, reuse only
+#                                          rocm/vllm-ci images and cache, and write no cache)
 #   Release pipeline:    its ECR repo     (never reads rocm/vllm-ci or its cache: it builds the
 #                                          stack and runtime from source, with only its own ECR cache;
 #                                          csrc objects come from the shared S3 sccache, as in CUDA)
+# Every untrusted build has the same rocm/vllm-dev credentials, so the prefixes keep names apart but
+# isolate nothing: any PR can overwrite another PR's tags and caches. Isolating PRs from each other
+# would take per-namespace credentials (ci-infra). The per-commit test image ($REPO:build-<id>) is
+# still pulled by tag, so a nightly's is PR-writable too until ci-infra pulls it by digest.
 # ROCM_CI_TRUSTED_REPO / ROCM_CI_CACHE_REPO only point a local run at a sandbox registry.
 set -euo pipefail
 
@@ -45,17 +51,17 @@ export BUILDKIT_PROGRESS=${BUILDKIT_PROGRESS:-plain}  # TTY progress redraws blo
 # PR builds write to a per-PR cache and prefix their image tags. The release pipeline's agents
 # cannot write rocm/vllm-ci or its cache: release writes its images and its own cache to $REPO,
 # so the next release reuses this one's all-arch compile.
-PFX=""
+PFX="" OWN=true
 if [[ $MODE == release* ]]; then
   CACHE="" CACHE_TO=$REPO:cache-   # and reads only that cache: CI agents also run PR code
 elif [[ $REPO != "$TRUSTED" ]]; then
   if [[ ${BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST:-false} != false ]]; then
-    PFX="pr$BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST-"
+    PFX="pr$BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST-" CACHE_TO=$REPO:cache-$PFX
   else   # not a PR (AITER nightly, branch or manual builds): one namespace per branch
     br=${BUILDKITE_BRANCH:-local}   # the hash keeps e.g. feat/x and feat-x apart
     PFX="br-$(printf %s "$br" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9.-' - | cut -c1-40)-$(printf %s "$br" | sha256sum | cut -c1-8)-"
+    CACHE_TO="" OWN=false   # any PR can write rocm/vllm-dev: never read back from it
   fi
-  CACHE_TO=$REPO:cache-$PFX
   # Only the compile stages' cache: everything else is cheap or in the trusted cache.
   export CACHE_CI=false
 fi
@@ -236,15 +242,17 @@ echo "build.sh $STACK $MODE: repo=$REPO trusted=$TRUSTED Ks=$Ks Kr=$Kr"
 #   1. Trusted registry (rocm/vllm-ci:<tag>) — safe for any CI build to reuse. Not for release:
 #      CI agents also run PR code, so release never ships an image it did not build itself.
 #   2. This repo's own tag ($REPO:$PFX<tag>) — PR builds and the release pipeline write here.
+#      Not for other untrusted builds (OWN=false): a PR could have pushed it.
 #   3. Main's key (MAIN_TAGS, untrusted base builds): wait for main's build of it, within a deadline.
 #   4. Otherwise: build via bake and push.
 # A <sibling-suffix> means the image only counts as present when the sibling
 # tag also exists (used by stack: must have both the image and -wheels); then
 # both pinned refs are printed, space-separated.
 ensure() {
   local target=$1 tag=$2 sibling=${3:-} ref d ds refs rc mf hb=""
-  refs=("$REPO:$PFX$tag")
-  [[ $MODE == release* || $REPO == "$TRUSTED" ]] || refs=("$TRUSTED:$tag" "${refs[@]}")
+  refs=()
+  [[ $MODE == release* || $REPO == "$TRUSTED" ]] || refs=("$TRUSTED:$tag")
+  [[ $OWN == false ]] || refs+=("$REPO:$PFX$tag")
 
   for ref in "${refs[@]}"; do
     if d=$(digest "$ref") && { [[ -z $sibling ]] || ds=$(digest "$ref$sibling"); }; then

@@ -445,14 +445,51 @@ RUN CARGO_BUILD_JOBS="$(nproc)" SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION="$(cat /tmp/vllm-
     bash tools/build_rust.sh \
     && test -x vllm/vllm-rs
 
+# What setup.py reads of pyproject.toml and vllm/envs.py: the project and setuptools tables, and the
+# variables setup.py names with the definitions they use (ast.unparse drops comments); vllm/__init__.py
+# only has to exist. COPY --from keys on content, so a new env var or lint rule no longer recompiles
+# all HIP code.
+FROM dev AS csrc-inputs
+COPY setup.py pyproject.toml vllm/envs.py /in/
+RUN cd /in && mkdir -p /out/vllm && : > /out/vllm/__init__.py \
+    && awk '/^\[/ { keep = /^\[(project|tool\.setuptools)/ } keep' pyproject.toml > /out/pyproject.toml \
+    && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 - <<'EOF'
+import ast, re
+setup, body = open("setup.py").read(), ast.parse(open("envs.py").read()).body
+def names(n):
+    targets = getattr(n, "targets", [getattr(n, "target", None)])
+    return {n.name} if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) else {t.id for t in targets if isinstance(t, ast.Name)}
+defs = {name: n for n in body for name in names(n)}
+table, words = defs["environment_variables"].value, set(re.findall(r"\w+", setup))
+table.keys, table.values = map(list, zip(*[kv for kv in zip(table.keys, table.values) if kv[0].value in words]))
+need, todo = set(), ["__getattr__", *re.findall(r"\benvs\.(\w+)", setup)]
+while todo:  # the module-level definitions those use, transitively
+    if (name := todo.pop()) in defs and name not in need:
+        need.add(name)
+        todo += [x.id for x in ast.walk(defs[name]) if isinstance(x, ast.Name)]
+keep = [n for n in body if isinstance(n, (ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom)) or names(n) & need]
+for n in keep:  # docstring edits must not recompile either
+    if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and ast.get_docstring(n):
+        n.body = n.body[1:] or [ast.Pass()]
+open("/out/vllm/envs.py", "w").write(ast.unparse(ast.Module(keep, [])))
+import importlib.util as u  # the filter must not change what setup.py reads
+def load(path):
+    spec = u.spec_from_file_location("envs", path)
+    spec.loader.exec_module(mod := u.module_from_spec(spec))
+    return mod
+orig, pruned = load("envs.py"), load("/out/vllm/envs.py")
+for n in sorted(set(re.findall(r"\benvs\.(\w+)", setup)) & set(orig.environment_variables)):
+    assert getattr(orig, n) == getattr(pruned, n), f"envs.{n} differs: update csrc-inputs in Dockerfile.rocm"
+EOF
+
 # Native extensions only: copies just the files that affect the HIP/C++ build (and the map tool).
 FROM triton-kernels AS csrc
 WORKDIR /app/vllm
-COPY setup.py CMakeLists.txt pyproject.toml ./
+COPY setup.py CMakeLists.txt ./
+COPY --from=csrc-inputs /out/ ./
 COPY tools/build_rust.py tools/build_rust.py
 COPY cmake cmake/
 COPY csrc csrc/
-COPY vllm/envs.py vllm/__init__.py vllm/
 # Empty: the stack's full PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH (release); CI passes the arches it can test.
 ARG ARCH
 # setup.py reads requirements/rocm.txt for install_requires. This wheel only carries the .so files

@@ -130,7 +130,7 @@ def run_build(
     fi ;;
   bake)
     echo "bake ${*:5}" >> "$CALLS"
-    echo "cache: ${CACHE:-own only}" >&2
+    echo "cache: ${CACHE:-own only}, to: ${CACHE_TO:-none}" >&2
     [[ $5 == --metadata-file ]] && for t in stack-rocm stack-wheels runtime test-deps
     do
       printf '  "%s": {\\n    "containerimage.digest": "sha256:%064d"\\n  },\\n' "$t" 1
@@ -239,13 +239,14 @@ def test_release_never_ships_images_from_the_ci_repo(tmp_path, mode):
     assert "vllm-ci-cache" not in stderr and "cache: own only" in stderr
 
 
-def test_ci_builds_reuse_the_trusted_images(tmp_path):
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("pull_request", ["7", "false"])
+def test_ci_builds_reuse_the_trusted_images(tmp_path, pull_request):
     status, stderr, calls = run_build(
         tmp_path,
         "base",
         ROCM_CI_REPO="rocm/vllm-dev",
         existing=TRUSTED_KEYED,
-        BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST="7",
+        BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST=pull_request,
     )
     assert status == 0, stderr
     assert not built_tags(calls, stderr)
@@ -275,6 +276,26 @@ def test_untrusted_builds_get_their_own_namespace(
     assert tags and all(t.startswith(f"rocm/vllm-dev:{prefix}") for t in tags)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("pull_request", "prefix"), [("7", "pr7-"), ("false", "br-")])
+def test_only_pr_builds_read_back_their_rocm_vllm_dev_namespace(
+    tmp_path, pull_request, prefix
+):
+    # Any PR can push to rocm/vllm-dev, e.g. the br-main- tags a nightly would reuse.
+    status, stderr, calls = run_build(
+        tmp_path,
+        "base",
+        ROCM_CI_REPO="rocm/vllm-dev",
+        existing=(f"rocm/vllm-dev:{prefix}",),
+        BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST=pull_request,
+    )
+    assert status == 0, stderr
+    is_pr = pull_request != "false"
+    assert (stderr.count("Reusing rocm/vllm-dev:") == 3) == is_pr
+    assert (len(built_tags(calls, stderr)) == 3) != is_pr
+    assert ("to: none" in stderr) != is_pr
+    assert is_pr or "cache: rocm/vllm-ci-cache" in stderr  # still reads main's cache
+
+
 def test_ci_build_uploads_the_kernel_symbol_map_when_asked(tmp_path):
     status, stderr, calls = run_ci_build(tmp_path, VLLM_KERNEL_SYMBOL_MAP="1")
     assert status == 0, stderr
